paper.core_task: Evaluating motion utilization in language-guided video segmentation via a motion-centric probing benchmark

contributions.name: A motion-centric benchmark for video segmentation probing
contributions.author_claim_text: we create a motion-centric probing and evaluation technique that questions previous efforts on motion referring expressions segmentation
contributions.description: A benchmark that pairs a static keyframe with a dynamic video clip to probe whether video MLLMs can differentiate genuine motion from static cues in language-guided segmentation.

contributions.name: Strong static-biased baselines for referring video segmentation
contributions.author_claim_text: we propose three strong baselines that outperform the state of the art while being static biased.
contributions.description: Three baselines using powerful multi-modal large language models (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL) combined with SAM 2.0, which achieve state-of-the-art performance while relying primarily on static information from a single image.

novelty_claims.text: - **Novel Benchmark Design:** The introduction of a motion-centric benchmark is innovative, offering a systematic way to probe models' ability to discern motion versus static cues.
Does this omission affect the novelty or relevance of the proposed baselines?
